issue_context.title: DeltaFIFO TransformFunc can result in a data race on re-sync
issue_context.body:
We use a `TransformFunc` to nil out the `ManagedFields`:

```
func(obj interface{}) (interface{}, error) {
    resourceUtil.MustToMeta(obj).SetManagedFields(nil)
    return obj, nil
})
```

However on a re-sync, this results in a data race that was observed when running unit tests:

```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c0006accc0 by goroutine 81:
  runtime.mapdelete_faststr()
      /usr/lib/golang/src/runtime/map_faststr.go:301 +0x0
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.RemoveNestedField()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go:274 +0x1e6
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.(*Unstructured).SetManagedFields()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/unstructured.go:476 +0x87
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.NewResourceSyncer.func3()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/syncer/resource_syncer.go:260 +0x4c
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*DeltaFIFO).queueActionLocked()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go:456 +0x101
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*DeltaFIFO).syncKeyLocked()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go:746 +0x154
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*DeltaFIFO).Resync()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go:717 +0x1b6
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*Reflector).startResync()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/reflector.go:378 +0x351
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache.(*Reflector).ListAndWatch.func2()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.29.3/tools/cache/reflector.go:356 +0x5d

Previous read at 0x00c0006accc0 by goroutine 82:
  runtime.mapaccess2_faststr()
      /usr/lib/golang/src/runtime/map_faststr.go:108 +0x0
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.NestedFieldNoCopy()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go:61 +0x10f
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.nestedMapNoCopy()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go:195 +0x66
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.NestedStringMap()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/helpers.go:167 +0x6e
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured.(*Unstructured).GetLabels()
      /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.29.3/pkg/apis/meta/v1/unstructured/unstructured.go:400 +0x94
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.getClusterIDLabel()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/syncer/resource_syncer.go:681 +0x65
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.(*resourceSyncer).shouldSync()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/syncer/resource_syncer.go:647 +0x4d
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.(*resourceSyncer).processNextWorkItem()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/syncer/resource_syncer.go:448 +0x3ad
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/syncer.(*resourceSyncer).processNextWorkItem-fm()
      <autogenerated>:1 +0x89
  github.com/submariner-io/admiral/pkg/workqueue.(*queueType).processNextWorkItem.func1()
      /go/pkg/mod/github.com/submariner-io/admiral@v0.18.0-m2.0.20240415195632-6c525b3cb5e9/pkg/workqueue/queue.go:103 +0x59
```

The read had occurred previously during a `ResourceEventHandler` callback.

On re-sync, the `DeltaFIFO` retrieves every object from the `knownObjects` cache,  invokes the transform function, and re-queues them.  However, the object instances are the same as those stored in the cache so mutating them outside the cache without lock protection is unsafe. It is documented that the "_TransformFunc sees the object before any other actor, and it is now safe to mutate the object in place instead of making a copy_" however this is not the case on a re-sync. The `DeltaFIFO` should make a copy of the objects retrieved from the cache store on a re-sync or perhaps elide the `TransformFunc` on a re-sync since the objects would already have been transformed.

As a workaround, I changed our `TransformFunc` to only nil the `ManagedFields` if not already nil but this is a latent bug that others will likely run into.

review_comments: I'm a little wary of this constraint. Consumers of the `TransformFunc` will not be aware of nor have control over how or where the object they receive came from. Nor should they care - that's an implementation detail of the `DeltaFIFO`. Also the `DeltaFIFO` itself does not have control over the origin of the objects from the upstream informers. I think it would be ideal for the `DeltaFIFO` to provide protection for the `TransformFunc` from potential data races. If an object already exists in the `knownObjects` cache and, more specifically, points to the same **instance** then make a copy of it before passing to the `TransformFunc`. The `TransformFunc` would then truly be free to mutate the object w/o any additional idempotency constraint. In fact we could go a step further and elide invoking the `TransformFunc` altogether in this case since we know the object came from the cache and was already transformed. Then we wouldn't really even need to special-case the tombstone or `Sync` action.

I agree that preventing more races is desired, however these for now these don't expose default usage of it. We should protect it further, but preventing existing issues seems more important to start with.

> however these for now these don't expose default usage of it.

I'm not clear on what you mean by this.

I think the text above would be a bit vague and confusing to users of the API. It would be for me if I hadn't studied the code and understand the issue and what it's trying say. With the changes in this PR, the potential race issue with passing cached objects to the `DeltaFIFO` could only occur with a custom informer and it's probably unlikely anyone is doing that so I'd omit this text. In fact, this should really documented as part of the `DeltaFIFO` API.

>> however these for now these don't expose default usage of it.
>
> I'm not clear on what you mean by this.

After the fix in this PR to omit Sync events and DeletedFinalStateUnknown objects, none of the uses of DeltaFIFO that client-go sets up (default informers / clients, etc) feed objects already present in `knownObjects` back into the transformer.

That means the only way a DeltaFIFO user would encounter that is if they wired up a non-default usage of DeltaFIFO to pass the same objects into DeltaFIFO multiple times as if they were new objects.

Someone doing that is presumably the same person wiring up the TransformFunc, and they need to understand the implications of what they are doing. Doing this effectively already breaks the *TransformFunc sees the object before any other actor, and it is now safe to mutate the object in place instead of making a copy.* statement / guarantee, so the TransformFunc author _must_ be aware of the implications of mutating objects it gets when they are being provided by something with different behavior than default client-go clients / informers.

> If an object already exists in the `knownObjects` cache and, more specifically, points to the same **instance** then make a copy of it before passing to the `TransformFunc`

The tracking / comparison cost to safeguard `TransformFunc` in that case is too high, and even if we did, `TransformFunc` would have to be aware of and protect against disrupting a non-default object provider.

I understand the reasoning. My point is that the `TransformFunc` is part of a higher-level API and is much more widely used and visible then the `DeltaFIFO`. The `New*Informer` functions are really the external-facing aspect of the `cache` module and I'm sure most users of these aren't even aware of `DeltaFIFO` and its semantics (I wasn't until I investigated this issue). As you mentioned, the author of a non-default usage of `DeltaFIFO`, if there are any, is "_presumably the same person wiring up the TransformFunc_", therefore document the constraints and implications re: caching and the `TransformFunc` in the `DeltaFIFO` API rather than here. This makes sense b/c the constraint that the `TransformFunc` be idempotent only applies if a non-default `DeltaFIFO` producer is used. As I said, I think the paragraph above will only confuse most people. Anyway, that's my 2 cents...
(and if we separately made our in-tree use of transformer idempotent, we'd avoid data race risks as well and that could maybe be narrowly picked to 1.29.x and 1.30.1 faster)

Done

And I will open a separate PR to make the functions idempotent.
